Flat even diagram lighting, a quiet nostalgic warmth. People are ordinary Lithuanians of 1981, anonymous types with correct natural proportions: fair skin, ash-blond to light-brown hair, grey or blue-grey eyes, broad-cheeked oval faces, straight noses, calm closed mouths, austere and plainly handsome. Men side-parted or cropped, some moustached, working men in flat caps; younger women lean, hair straight or faintly waved; older women with set or curled hair or a cotton headscarf; plain loose clothes in brown, olive, dusty blue, grey and dull red. Heads turn at varied natural angles, as in a documentary photograph; one or two face the viewer, eyes resting just past the viewer's shoulder. Subject: a worker walking forward in mid-stride. Motion strip of three clearly different phases of the same man: standing with feet together; left leg forward, right arm forward; right leg forward, left arm forward. Arrow in solid black ink. Show the worker performing the action large and clear in the foreground, floating on the cream paper WITHOUT any hard box or border around the main scene, set within a long institutional corridor, the figure walking to the right, with a little quiet civic activity in the background that fades softly into the paper. Include one bold arrow pointing to the RIGHT, the exact way the figure faces and steps (arrow and motion the same direction). Only include people the subject or scene actually calls for; do not add an extra standing figure that is not needed. Beneath the main scene, in small bordered panels, include a clean civic procedural sequence of two or three panels showing the simple motion of the action step by step. You MAY add one small Lithuanian tricolor flag. Nothing else — keep it uncluttered. Use external close-up details instead. (A simple sliced view of a fruit or plain object is fine.)
